guarantees.claim: For each i in 0..3, data_in_mask[i] is continuously assigned aes_prd_get_lsbs(prd_sub_bytes[i * WidthPRDRow +: WidthPRDRow]).

assumptions.claim: prd_sub_bytes has at least 4 * WidthPRDRow bits, ensuring the slice [i * WidthPRDRow +: WidthPRDRow] is within bounds.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds indexing causes X propagation or simulation error, potentially corrupting mask values.

assumptions.claim: aes_prd_get_lsbs returns a vector whose width matches data_in_mask[i] (likely WidthPRDRow), and correctly extracts the LSBs.
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch leads to truncation or zero-extension, breaking the masking scheme.

uncertain_points.claim: The mask data_in_mask is derived from prd_sub_bytes, which may come from a PRD block with unknown reseeding or freshness guarantees; static or predictable values would compromise the intended masking of AES data.
uncertain_points.risk: Predictable or stale mask exposes secret intermediate values to side-channel or fault attacks.

uncertain_points.claim: data_in_mask is assigned combinationaly and may change asynchronously relative to the AES datapath; there is no explicit handshake or gating to ensure the mask is stable during a cryptographic round.
uncertain_points.risk: Unstable mask could cause incorrect unmasking or correlation leakage.
